BaseIdentity.description:
The spec1 identity-core projection document for one Spec: exactly what
gets hashed to produce its spec_id, serialised once and echoed back
verbatim -- never re-derived by a second, parallel implementation.

Every Spec carries one, on `Spec.definition.identity` (see
`SpecDefinition`). A dataset_resubmit identity entry posts a prior Spec's own
`definition.identity` byte-for-byte as its edited `identity`. Directional
entities live directly in `identity.entities.origin` and
`identity.entities.destination`. StatVar members are graph state, derived from the
identity, and no member here.

The document is hashed whole. `"spec_"` plus the first 32 hex digits of
the SHA-256 of its RFC 8785 serialisation, with null members omitted, is
the Spec's spec_id.

identity_version.description: the identity domain separator this Spec was hashed under
identity_version.title: Identity Version

shape.description: the shape this Spec was hashed under
shape.title: Shape

slots.description: the what/how slots that feed identity -- where/when/source are excluded
slots.title: Slots

entities.description: the bound entities, keyed by role (observationAbout/origin/destination); {} when none were bound -- always present, never omitted. A role that appears carries at least one dcid: the identity core refuses a role with zero members, so an empty list must not be expressible here
entities.title: Entities

requested_window.description: the requested date window this Spec was hashed under; always present -- {"kind": "all"} means no date was requested at all
requested_window.title: Requested Window

facets.description: sparse facet bindings (provenance/measurementMethod/unit); omitted entirely when no facet axis is bound, never an empty object. A facet axis that appears is bound -- value, set, or (unit axis only) the request form -- never unbound: the identity core refuses an unbound facet binding state, since a sparse map omits what is not bound rather than carrying it as unbound
facets.title: Facets

open_roles.description: the flow axes asked for member by member (every creditor, every donor), sorted and de-duplicated; omitted when none is. A role absent from both entities and open_roles asks for the total over that role. An open role is never also an entities key, and a pinned shape (kind='stat_var') carries none
open_roles.title: Open Roles

BaseIdentity.title: BaseIdentity

DatasetResubmitInput.description:
Re-resolve every part of a multi-variable result in one request, so an
edit to one part cannot leave the other parts' composed sentence or fold
stale (see `envelope.make_response` / `conjoin.combine_regions`, the
combiner every entry kind here is routed through).

`entries` supplies one entry per response part, in response part order;
each entry edits against its own base, never a dataset-level one. There
is no spec registry, so every entry carries its full identity and this
door reads no server-side state.

kind.description: discriminator for dataset-level re-resolution across every part
kind.title: Kind

entries.description: one entry per response part, in response part order; a single-entry request whose entry is an identity re-resolves exactly that one part
entries.title: Entries

raw_query.description: original query text, for echo only; does not affect resolution
raw_query.title: Raw Query

DatasetResubmitInput.title: DatasetResubmitInput

EntityGroup.description:
A named group whose members fill one entity role, as the request named it
("EU member states"). The members themselves are the role's dcids in
`BaseIdentity.entities`. This records only that they were asked for as one
group, so the heading can say "the 27 EU member states" after any edit that
keeps the role's members. A group the graph holds no node for, read from the
membership registry ("Asia (DAC)"), names the registry's id for it in
`group_id`, so a resubmit restores it and the total its dataset publishes for it.
A group whose `ref` is a continent or subregion
that the membership policy holds or omits (`MembershipPolicy.holds_region`)
reads as its countries ("the 54 countries in Africa"), whatever its graph
type. `entity_type` is informational, and the reading keys on `ref`. When
the role binds the total its dataset publishes
for the group ("Africa (DAC)") in place of the members, `total` names that
party and the role's one dcid is it. A Spec serves its groups on
`ResolvedSpec.entity_groups`, and a resubmit posts them beside the identity
(`ResubmitIdentityEntry.entity_groups`, `ResubmitCandidate.entity_groups`).

ref.description: the group's own graph node, when the graph holds one; null otherwise
ref.title: Ref

label.description: the group's name as the request gave it, plain text
label.title: Label

entity_type.description: the graph type of the group's own node, e.g. Continent, UNGeoRegion, ContinentalUnion; null when the graph holds no node for the group
entity_type.title: Entity Type

total.description: the party the dataset publishes as the group's total, which the role binds in place of the members (DACAfrica for Africa); null when the role binds the members
total.title: Total

group_id.description: the membership registry's id for a group the graph holds no node for, e.g. groups/OECD.DAC.Region.Asia; null when ref is set or the group is no registry group
group_id.title: Group Id

EntityGroup.title: EntityGroup

IdentityBindingExact.description:
A single bound dcid, denoting that code alone -- never its subtree,
even where the code is a hierarchical (non-leaf) code (see
`docs/identity-v1.md` in `spec-kit` for the denotation rule: `value`
denotes a hierarchical code's whole subtree, `exact` denotes the code
alone). Slot-only: `_build_facet_binding` refuses `exact` on a facet.
No engine `Binding` arm maps onto this state and no minting site
produces it -- see `IdentityBinding`'s own docstring.

The role-shaped form of a unit request's `currency`: the currency of
the entity bound to this spec role, resolved per row. Field-for-field mirror

IdentityFacetValueAbsent.description:
A measurementMethod or unit facet bound to no declared value:
`{"state": "value", "ref": null}` asks for the facets that declare no value
on the axis, the ones Data Commons serves without that member. An unbound
axis admits every facet; this binding admits only those without a value.
Mirrors the identity core's null facet ref (`docs/identity-v1.md` in
`spec-kit`). `ref` serialises as `null` even under `exclude_none`, since
the identity core refuses a value binding with neither `ref` nor `request`.

ref.description: null: the facet declares no value on this axis
ref.title: Ref

IdentityFacetValueRequest.description:
A unit-axis facet bound via the request form: "serve whatever facet
honours this completed currency/prices/base_year request" rather than a
literal graph ref. `state` reuses the value-state spelling since this is
still a single-valued binding to the identity core -- `request` is what
distinguishes it from `IdentityBindingValue`'s `ref` form (see
`_facet_binding_tag`, this union's discriminator).
IdentityFacetValueRequest.title: IdentityFacetValueRequest

ref.description: the resolved denominator StatVar's dcid
ref.title: Ref

The described arm's `measurement_denominator`, present on the graph but
never resolved to a dcid (e.g. a dcid-less ProvisionalNode) -- distinct
from the member being absent entirely, which means no denominator arc
exists at all.

unresolved.description: always the literal true -- the arc exists but names no dcid
unresolved.title: Unresolved

IdentityShapePin.description:
The pinned-ask arm of the identity core's `shape` union
(`kind: "stat_var"`): a single StatVar dcid, minted by Datasets'
statvar_set. See `BaseIdentity`'s cross-member validator -- when this arm
is chosen, `slots` must be empty.
IdentityShapePin.title: IdentityShapePin

IdentityShapeSchema.description:
The described-ask arm of the identity core's `shape` union
(`kind: "statvar_schema"`): up to five sparse schema members mapping 1:1
onto Search's FiveTuple (see `engine.shape.identity_shape_for`, the
adapter that builds this from a ShapeDraft's or a grounded wire Shape's
five-tuple dcids). Minted by Search for every standard and family shape.

Every member is optional and sparse -- an absent member contributes no
bytes, the same sparse rule the facets map follows -- but an arm
describing nothing is invalid: at least one member must be present (see
`_at_least_one_schema_member`).

stat_type.description: the graph statType dcid, e.g. measuredValue
stat_type.title: Stat Type

measurement_qualifier.description: the graph measurementQualifier dcid, present only when the measured property is qualified
measurement_qualifier.title: Measurement Qualifier

measurement_denominator.description: the graph measurementDenominator, present only on a ratio or per-capita measure: {'ref': dcid} when resolved, {'unresolved': true} when the arc exists but names no dcid
measurement_denominator.title: Measurement Denominator

IdentityShapeSchema.title: IdentityShapeSchema

IdentitySlot.description:
One what/how slot's identity contribution: property dcid + binding state.

Never a where/when/source slot: `where` is carried by entity roles instead,
`when` is carried by `requested_window` instead, and `source` is carried by
`facets.provenance` instead -- all three would otherwise hash resolved
graph state rather than what was actually asked. Every IdentitySlot here
carries a real constraint property by construction of the shape grammar.
IdentitySlot.title: IdentitySlot

IdentityUnitRequest.description:
A completed unit-conversion request, in the identity core's own wire
shape (`dfo_spec_kit.identity`'s `_build_unit_request`) -- legal only
inside a unit-axis facet binding's `request` member
(`IdentityFacetValueRequest`; see `BaseIdentity`'s model validator, which
refuses this form on any other axis).

Field-for-field mirror of the identity core's own `_UNIT_REQUEST_KEYS`
schema: `currency` is upper-case ISO 4217 or a role object naming
the spec role whose bound entity's currency to use (see
`IdentityCurrency`; the identity core NFC-normalises a string spelling
but does not case-fold, so a lower-case currency refuses here rather
than silently normalising to a different meaning at hash time), `prices`
is current (nominal) or constant (real, anchored to
`base_year`), and `base_year` is present exactly when `prices=="constant"`
-- both directions enforced below, matching the identity core's own
`invalid_unit_request` pair of checks. `base_year` is `StrictInt`,
matching `_require_integral_number`'s own exclusion of `bool` (a Python
`int` subclass) and of numeric strings -- a lax `int` field would coerce
JSON `true` to `1` and `"2023"` to `2023`, hashing a malformed request
under an unintended base year instead of refusing it. Under simultaneous
violations
(e.g. a lower-case currency together with a missing base_year) the two
layers can report a different invariant first: this model's per-field
`currency` pattern validates ahead of `_base_year_matches_prices` (a
`mode="after"` validator, which never runs once a field has already
failed), while the identity core checks `prices`-vs-`base_year` before
the currency regex. Same HTTP status/code either way -- message content
only.

currency.description: the requested currency, upper-case ISO 4217 (e.g. 'USD'), or a role object
currency.title: Currency

base_year.description: required exactly when prices=='constant'; absent when prices=='current'
base_year.title: Base Year

IdentityUnitRequest.title: IdentityUnitRequest

IdentityWindowAll.description: No date signal was requested at all.
IdentityWindowAll.title: IdentityWindowAll

IdentityWindowLatest.description: An explicit latest-ask: re-resolve to whatever year is CURRENTLY latest.
IdentityWindowLatest.title: IdentityWindowLatest

IdentityWindowRange.description: A concrete requested date range; at least one bound is always present.
IdentityWindowRange.title: IdentityWindowRange

Operation.description:
One computation the question asks for over a part's data, which search
does not perform: the part answers with the data the operation needs, and
the operation rides on the part for a client to perform or hand on.

verb.description: what the question asks to compute: rank, aggregate, growth, share_of, explain, forecast, or report
verb.title: Verb

phrase.description: the query wording that asks for the operation, e.g. 'top 5 donors'; one line with no control characters or line separators, and not blank
phrase.title: Phrase

over.description: the axis the operation runs across (place, origin, destination, category, or year); null when the verb names none, as explain does. The part leaves this axis open, so its data covers every value the operation needs
over.title: Over

target_year.description: the year a forecast projects to, e.g. 2050 for 'forecast aid to Ethiopia to 2050'; set only on a forecast, a four-digit year up to 2200. The raw_text door sets it only to a year after the current one, and leaves it null when the question names none; a posted value is taken as given within the bound, whatever today's date. It is kept apart from the part's time_text, the years whose data the part fetches, and does not affect resolution
target_year.title: Target Year

Operation.title: Operation

ParsedEntity.description: One entity mentioned in a parsed part, with an optional caller-supplied role hint.

text.description: the entity's text as the caller identified it
text.title: Text

role_text.description: the caller's free-form role hint for this entity, when available; recognised words (case-insensitive) are 'from'/'to' and synonyms such as donor/provider/funder/source/creditor/lender/exporter for the 'from' side, recipient/beneficiary/debtor/borrower/importer for the 'to' side -- unrecognised text warns role_text_not_recognised and the entity is treated as undirected
role_text.title: Role Text

dcid.description: an optional caller-pinned dcid for this entity, naming exactly which graph node `text` refers to -- the door a client with a candidate's dcid in hand (e.g. from NoData.ambiguous_entities) posts through, instead of relying on name resolution to disambiguate `text` on its own. When present, this entity's name resolution is skipped: the pinned dcid seeds the entry's pre_resolved map directly, still confirmed against the graph. An unconfirmable dcid (absent from the graph, or present but type-less) refuses invalid_role_ref (422). `text` stays required and is not re-derived from the dcid; it is still what a rendered sentence and any further restatement echo back.
dcid.title: Dcid

members.description: true asks for the members of the set `text` names, each as its own series: the countries of a continent or UN subregion, or the members of a group. It has no effect on a single place. Text whose wording names members, such as 'EU member states', reads as true without the flag. With a pinned `dcid` it is honoured for a continent or subregion that the membership policy holds or omits, whatever the node's graph type, and refuses request_invalid for a group's own node, whose members a pin cannot supply. One part names a set once: the same `text` posted with both values refuses request_invalid
members.title: Members

skipping natural-language extraction.

parts.title: Parts

ParsedPart.description: One variable ask within a parsed request, with its own entities, time, unit, and source.

variable_text.description: the variable's text as the caller identified it
variable_text.title: Variable Text

entities.description: entities associated with this part's variable, when available; null, omitted, or an empty list all mean no entity was named for this part, resolving the variable globally/entity-less -- the same meaning a raw_text query with no extracted place carries
entities.title: Entities

time_text.description: this part's time expression, when available; recognised forms include a bare four-digit year, 'YYYY to YYYY' or 'YYYY-YYYY', 'from YYYY to YYYY', 'between YYYY and YYYY', a latest end as in 'between YYYY and the latest' or 'YYYY to latest', 'since YYYY', 'latest', 'latest year available', 'most recent', and 'last N years'. Anything else resolves dateless with a time_text_not_parsed warning, whose message lists every form
time_text.title: Time Text

unit_text.description: this part's requested unit or measurement basis, when available; recognised phrasing names a currency (ISO 4217 code or curated name/alias), a price basis (current or constant prices), and/or a base year (e.g. '2015 US dollars', 'constant prices, 2015 base year'). A phrase this text failed to parse cleanly resolves no_data with unit_not_resolved; a phrase the request grammar cannot express at all resolves unsupported with unit_request_unsupported. A phrase the grammar CAN express is checked against this deployment's own unit data: a currency/prices/base_year combination no unit this deployment carries expresses at all resolves unsupported with facet_binding_unsupported; one this deployment can express but that matches no candidate observation resolves no_data with facet_not_available; a match resolves definite, applying the completed request to the resolved spec's identity and carrying request_basis on resolved.facets.unit
unit_text.title: Unit Text

sources.description: the data sources this part names or excludes, in query order. Empty, the part answers from the sources the engine elects. A restatement echoes each mention with the reference it resolved to
sources.title: Sources

source_text.description: deprecated: post `sources` instead. Read as one included mention with this text, appended to `sources`
source_text.title: Source Text

provenance.title: Provenance

source_code.description: a publisher's own series code for this part's variable, such as the World Bank's DT.TDS.DEGG.CD, when the user or a skill gives one. Compared upper-cased, it names the variables the publisher gives that code, and the part answers from them in place of matching variable_text; variable_text, entities and open_roles still choose among them. A code is never a constraint and narrows nothing else. A code whose variables cannot answer the part, because no source search serves holds it, the part's sources leave out every source holding it, or its variables cannot answer the part as asked, resolves no_data with source_code_not_held, its message naming the cause; a code two of the part's sources hold resolves no_data with source_code_ambiguous until `sources` names one; a code whose variable another code of its source also names resolves no_data with source_code_shares_variable, naming those codes

operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none
operations.title: Operations

open_roles.description: the roles this part asks for member by member, at most one word per flow axis, e.g. ['creditor'] for 'debt service paid to each creditor'. Each is a role_text word: creditor, donor, recipient, debtor, origin, destination, or a synonym. Where the answer's family declares the role, the answer holds one series per member of it and its identity states the axis in open_roles; a role named in neither entities nor open_roles reads as the total over that role. An unrecognised word, or a role one of this part's entities binds through role_text, refuses request_invalid. An operation whose over is origin or destination opens that axis too
open_roles.title: Open Roles

separate.description: true when this part is asked beside the others to be compared with them, as in 'health ODA versus education ODA': it answers as its own part and never folds into another part of the same shape (binding_folded). False, the default, folds parts that share a shape into one set answer
separate.title: Separate

ResolveOptions.description: Optional resolution parameters the caller may supply.

include_option_coverage.description: when true, the engine probes each top-level interpretation and candidate Spec's slot_options for observation coverage (e.g. 'Kenya — 205 obs') and populates SlotOption.coverage; false/absent (the default) never fires the extra probes, so this is opt-in latency, not a hidden cost on the hot path. Delivery differs by transport, for every input kind: over SSE (Accept: text/event-stream), coverage arrives via trailing slot_options/entity_options events emitted after the response event, and the response event's own Spec.resolved.slot_options / entity_options stay coverage=null; on the buffered JSON body, coverage is embedded directly in the returned Spec. Spec.resolved.facet_options is computed whether or not this is set; over SSE with this set, it arrives in trailing facet_options events instead of the response event.
include_option_coverage.title: Include Option Coverage

include_observations.description: when true (the default is false -- absent also means false), the engine populates Spec.resolved.observations with the resolved answer's observation values: the full series when small enough, otherwise a bounded latest-points preview. This per-spec fetch runs only after the engine commits to a definite spec, including a promoted candidate; a multi-candidate response keeps per-candidate metadata and coverage without fetching observations. Delivery mirrors include_option_coverage's transport split: over SSE, observations arrive via a trailing observations event emitted after the response event, and the response event's own Spec.resolved.observations stays null or omitted; on the buffered JSON body, observations are embedded directly in the returned Spec.
include_observations.title: Include Observations

include_skills.description: when true (the default is false -- absent also means false), the engine matches every resolved Spec's bound graph nodes (its shape's structural anchors and the dcids its bound constraint slots name) and its selected provenance (facets.provenance.ref, when one provenance serves every series) against the shared skills index and populates Spec.resolved.skills with the matching skill ids: skills matched through a graph node first, nearest-attachment-first, then skills matched only through the provenance, by id; [] when nothing matched. The response's own skills map then carries every named skill's front matter once, keyed by id. When the shared skills index has not yet built a first snapshot, the response carries the skills_index_unavailable diagnostics warning instead and no Spec gets a populated skills field; when a snapshot is available but its own build may have left out a published skill or served one excluded or understated (a read stopped at a budget or bound, the build's content budget ran out before a skill's turn, or a build step failed), the response instead carries the skills_index_incomplete diagnostics warning alongside whatever matches it did serve; a part with no resolved spec (no_data, unsupported) carries the part-scoped skills_not_matchable warning, since it binds no graph nodes to match against.
include_skills.title: Include Skills

identities, through the promote path, in posted order, always. `ordering`
names the display rule this set already used, restated rather than
recomputed: the order rests on the bind model's election and the availability
reads of the first answer, which do not round-trip -- see `Ordering` and
`outcomes.CandidateSet`. This entry carries no
`max_candidates` field: `CandidateSet.max_candidates` on the response is
not posted back and is always server-computed, never client-supplied.

BaseIdentity.description:
The spec1 identity-core projection document for one Spec: exactly what
gets hashed to produce its spec_id, serialised once and echoed back
verbatim -- never re-derived by a second, parallel implementation.

Every Spec carries one, on `Spec.definition.identity` (see
`SpecDefinition`). A dataset_resubmit identity entry posts a prior Spec's own
`definition.identity` byte-for-byte as its edited `identity`. Directional
entities live directly in `identity.entities.origin` and
`identity.entities.destination`. StatVar members are graph state, derived from the
identity, and no member here.

The document is hashed whole. `"spec_"` plus the first 32 hex digits of
the SHA-256 of its RFC 8785 serialisation, with null members omitted, is
the Spec's spec_id.

CandidateSet.description:
A set of 2..N competing Specs, presented in the order named by ``ordering``.

``ordering="intent_rank"``: the order the status rule offers the readings in. A first
answer always uses it. The elected reading comes first, then its rivals in menu order,
each stating why it is offered (``ResolvedSpec.basis``). Where the elected reading holds
no data and several siblings differing from it only on the measurement qualifier do,
those siblings are the set, in menu order, without it. Where a place named without a
direction holds data under both, the elected reading under each direction is offered.

``ordering="broadest_first"``: a posted candidates entry that names it
(``ResubmitCandidatesEntry``) keeps its posted order and states this ordering back. No
first answer uses it.

Each candidate carries its own heading and byline inside its own
``resolved.rendered_sentence``/``resolved.sentence_plan``. There is no separate parallel sentence array, and a
candidate's Spec is a returned Spec like any other. The part's own
sentence opens with how many readings there are and states, for each
shown candidate, the source and span that set it apart.

Departure.description:
One way this part's answer differs from what its request asked, stated
for people in `text` and for code in `code`, `asked`, and `shown`.

Departures live on the part (`_PartBase.departures`).
`spec.resolved.rendered_sentence` states what the answer is, and a
departure states how that differs from the request that produced it.

code.description: what kind of departure this is. 'closest_match': the answer shows the nearest measure the graph holds, not the one asked; a client draws a muted 'Closest match:' lead before the heading, and on a candidates part, whose readings stand in for a measure with no data, once before the first reading. 'measure_not_applied': a named measure qualifier was not applied. 'operation_not_applied': an operation the request named (a share, a ranking) was not run, so the amounts behind it are shown. 'breakdown_not_applied': a breakdown the request named was not applied, so the total is shown. 'entity_unavailable': an entity the request named holds no values in the series the answer reads, one departure per role; for a role the request named as a group, asked is the request's words for the group and the text counts the members without values; the text names any source holding values there that Search does not read. 'year_unavailable': a named year or range falls outside the years served. 'modelled_values': the served values are modelled or estimated. 'group_read_as_members': a named group was read as its member entities; on a flow role the text names the amounts the group's published total counts that no member holds, and, for a group whose published total is not its members' sum, says the source publishes its own figure for the group. 'direction_discarded': a flow direction the request's own words named was not applied. 'direction_inferred': a place the request named without a direction is read on the one direction that holds data, which over names. 'scope_limited': a no_data answer's check covered only values the engine chose, which the request did not name; its text names only what the check covered ('This check covered only ODA.')

A named group whose members fill one entity role, as the request named it

Headline.description:
The exact, one-year summary of a role-bearing answer's own served
population: the year `CoverageIndex.headline` (series_coverage) heads the
answer with, whether that year was the one the question named, the exact
observation and series count in that year alone, and how many distinct dcids
each role carries in it. `series_coverage.index.Headline`'s own docstring is
the source of truth for why `observations` and `series` are always equal
under this schema.

The counts are those of the year the answer's read plan serves. Under a `latest`
window that is the year its variables elect (`CoverageIndex.elected_years`), which
the preview and a mint of the Spec serve too. Under a named window it is the latest
year with data in that window, so a question naming 2015 to 2020 counts the latest
of those years with data. `named_window` carries the years it named.

Attached to every role-bearing answer (named-destination confirmed and
open-axis discovered alike), never to a non-role-bearing one: coverage
only exists for role-bearing series (series_coverage.schema's own scope
note), and computing this is a free in-memory bitmask operation, not a
network read, so there is no population-size reason to withhold it from
a narrow answer the way the per-series preview stays capped at 20
regardless of how broad the answer is.

year.description: the year the counts are for. For a latest window it is the elected year: of the three calendar years ending at the newest year a variable's series hold, at or before the year the coverage artifact was built, the newest one that at least half as many series hold as the fullest of the three, and with several variables the newest year any of them elects. For a named window it is the latest year any served series has an observation inside the window
year.title: Year

year_named.description: whether the request itself named a year or a range of years, rather than defaulting to one, independent of whether those years include the shown `year`
year_named.title: Year Named

named_window.description: the year or years the request named: equal bounds for one year, an absent bound for an open range; null when no year was named. The counts are for `year` alone, whatever this window holds

observations.description: exact observation count across served series in year
observations.title: Observations

series.description: exact series count with an observation in year
series.title: Series

role_counts.description: distinct dcid count per role active in year, keyed by the graph's own role property dcid (e.g. financingProvider, financingRecipient) -- never by a donor/recipient label, so the wire stays aligned with Data Commons' own names
role_counts.title: Role Counts

recent_years.description: the counts for three calendar years, newest first, so a newest year with far fewer series than the years before it reads as incomplete. For a latest window they are raw counts over every series the answer holds, ending at the newest year any of them holds at or before the year the coverage artifact was built, or at the newest year any holds when none holds a year that early; `year` is one of the three: the newest year a variable heads, which is the year it elected or, for a variable that elects none, such as one of monthly data, its newest year at or before the build year. When no variable holds a year that early, each heads its newest year. `observations`, `series` and `role_counts` count only the variables heading it. For a named window they end at `year`, the first entry repeats `observations`, `series` and `role_counts`, and the earlier years count whether or not `named_window` reaches them. A year with no data is kept with zero counts. The list stops at the first year the coverage artifact represents, so it can hold fewer than three entries
recent_years.title: Recent Years

`facets.provenance` instead -- all three would otherwise hash resolved

IdentityUnitRequest.description:
A completed unit-conversion request, in the identity core's own wire
shape (`dfo_spec_kit.identity`'s `_build_unit_request`) -- legal only
inside a unit-axis facet binding's `request` member
(`IdentityFacetValueRequest`; see `BaseIdentity`'s model validator, which
refuses this form on any other axis).

Field-for-field mirror of the identity core's own `_UNIT_REQUEST_KEYS`
schema: `currency` is upper-case ISO 4217 or a role object naming
the spec role whose bound entity's currency to use (see
`IdentityCurrency`; the identity core NFC-normalises a string spelling
but does not case-fold, so a lower-case currency refuses here rather
than silently normalising to a different meaning at hash time), `prices`
is current (nominal) or constant (real, anchored to
`base_year`), and `base_year` is present exactly when `prices=="constant"`
-- both directions enforced below, matching the identity core's own
`invalid_unit_request` pair of checks. `base_year` is `StrictInt`,
matching `_require_integral_number`'s own exclusion of `bool` (a Python
`int` subclass) and of numeric strings -- a lax `int` field would coerce
JSON `true` to `1` and `"2023"` to `2023`, hashing a malformed request
under an unintended base year instead of refusing it. Under simultaneous
violations
(e.g. a lower-case currency together with a missing base_year) the two
layers can report a different invariant first: this model's per-field
`currency` pattern validates ahead of `_base_year_matches_prices` (a
`mode="after"` validator, which never runs once a field has already
failed), while the identity core checks `prices`-vs-`base_year` before
the currency regex. Same HTTP status/code either way -- message content
only.

base_year.description: required exactly when prices=='constant'; absent when prices=='current'
base_year.title: Base Year

NearestRealSpec.description:
A nearest_real suggestion: a full Spec found by relaxing one constraint
binding and re-confirming the result against the live graph.

Graph-re-confirmed only, never fabricated. See relaxation for which
binding was dropped to find it.

spec_id.description: deterministic hash of (shape + canonical slot bindings); permalink-safe, dedup key, golden-comparison handle, cache key
spec_id.title: Spec Id

definition.description: the canonical definition this Spec was resolved from: {schema_version, identity}, the same shape Unsupported.definition uses. definition.identity is the identity-core projection this spec_id was minted from, serialised once and never re-derived; hashing it reproduces spec_id by construction. Post definition.identity back byte-for-byte as ResubmitIdentityPayload.identity to edit this Spec. Directional entities remain nested in identity.entities.

resolved.description: the engine's report of what it did with the ask: stat_vars, entities, coverage, trace, and every other display/diagnostic field. Never hashed; see ResolvedSpec

relaxation.description: the definition part this suggestion relaxed, and the value(s) it dropped

NearestRealSpec.title: NearestRealSpec

NoData.description: Outcome when no grounded result can be returned.

reason.description: why nothing could be returned, in contract resolution order. "entity_not_resolved" means a named entity could not be resolved to a graph node; "entity_ambiguous" means a named entity matched more than one graph candidate and none could be preferred over the others, distinct from "entity_not_resolved", where no node matched at all; "entity_role_not_admitted" means a named entity resolved to exactly one graph node, but no role any candidate shape declares admits that node's graph type -- the entity is real, just not the kind of thing this query's data is reported for; "entity_set_too_large" means every named entity resolved, but the places the request names, counting the members of each group or region among them and summed over the roles they sit on, exceed what the engine binds in one request -- distinct from every other entity_* reason, where one entity, not the size of the set, is what failed; "variable_not_resolved" means no StatVar matched the variable text (e.g. an absent posted stat_var_dcid or entity, or no measure match at all); "role_not_resolved" means the query names a role the engine could not resolve; "unit_not_resolved" means the unit binder could not classify a token in the requested unit phrase against its lexicons; "no_matching_slice" means the measure matched fine, but the requested combination has no corresponding data series -- the constructed/derived variable does not exist in the graph at all. Covers an identity resubmit refine edit with no confirmable sibling StatVar for the edited slice, and a dev-finance scheme x purpose x recipient combination that was never published as a series, on raw-text and resubmit alike; "binding_mismatch" means the variable resolved and graph-confirmed StatVars exist, but none satisfies the requested slot bindings, either because a resolved value on a bound property mismatched or because the StatVar's value on a bound property is present but could not be read (an unresolvable dcid); distinct from "no_matching_slice" (the combination was never published at all) and "variable_not_resolved" (no StatVar matched at all); "denominator_not_available" means the query asks for a normalised form (per person, per area, a rate or a share) or names a denominator, and the matched series is not in that form or divides by another base; "no_observations" means a StatVar WAS confirmed to exist but has no observation at the resolved entity (it exists, but not data here); "facet_not_available" means observations exist at the entity, none under the requested facet values; "role_incompatible" means the role is real, and the StatVar does not declare it; "role_signature_incompatible" means the resolved StatVars carry incompatible role signatures and no partition into candidates was possible; "source_code_not_held" means no variable held under the part's source_code by a source search serves can answer the part: no served source holds the code, the part's sources exclude every source that does, or the code's variables cannot answer the part as asked; "source_code_ambiguous" means two of the part's sources hold its source_code; "source_code_shares_variable" means the source_code's variables answer other codes of its source too, so search cannot serve the code alone; "qualifier_not_bound" means the variable resolved to a series family, but a narrowing term the request's text named bound no constraint slot: no code system in the packaged index carries it, or its registered rows landed in no binding
reason.title: Reason

cause.description: why this refusal fired, present only for reason=rate_coverage_gap (the structured door's same-named ProblemDetails extension); omitted on every other reason

category.description: derived from reason, never independently settable: "entity_not_resolved", "entity_ambiguous", "entity_set_too_large", "entity_role_not_admitted", "variable_not_resolved", "role_not_resolved", "source_not_resolved", "source_ambiguous", "source_code_not_held", "source_code_ambiguous", "source_code_shares_variable", and "unit_not_resolved" are "unresolved" (the request could not be read into the graph); every other code is "absent" (the read request names a place holding nothing)
category.title: Category

message.description: the plain-language sentence for reason, naming the query terms it concerns where the reason has them (the indicator, place, or category wording), so a client can show a person the reason beside its code. Every no_data part the engine returns sets it. Clients must not parse it
message.title: Message

nearest_real.description: optional; up to two real, grounded specs found by relaxing one constraint at a time and re-confirming against the live graph. Each carries its own relaxation naming the definition part relaxed and the value(s) it dropped. Shaped by response_options and banded by confidence like any returned spec. Distinct from flagged_match (the elected variable itself) and alternate_match (a different variable). nearest_real varies the SAME variable's own constraints, never the variable.
nearest_real.title: Nearest Real

gate.description: optional; the failed quality gate's code from the platform registry, one of the three registry gate codes (no_member_has_data_at_place, no_member_asserts_bound_properties, only_alternate_has_data). The single home for the code regardless of which near-match field carries the Spec: present exactly when flagged_match or alternate_match is present, except a role_incompatible refusal before or during materialise whose flagged_match records the confirmed elected identity without a gate (role incompatibility prevents an availability verdict), a qualifier_not_bound refusal, whose flagged_match records the graph-confirmed elected spec without a gate because the qualifier guard refuses before an availability verdict exists, or a denominator_not_available refusal, whose flagged_match records the elected spec the form or denominator check refused. Absent on every other no_data outcome. At most one of flagged_match and alternate_match is present at a time.
gate.title: Gate

flagged_match.description: optional; the elected variable's own Spec, present whenever gate fired and a groundable identity exists for the elected shape, or for a role_incompatible, qualifier_not_bound or denominator_not_available refusal that records its graph-confirmed identity without a gate: role incompatibility prevents an availability verdict, the qualifier guard refuses before one exists, and the denominator check refuses the series for its form, not its data. See gate for which check failed. available_at_place is False and confidence is low on gate=no_member_has_data_at_place; both stay at their not-assessed default (None) on gate=no_member_asserts_bound_properties, since there is no resolved place to be unavailable at. Absent on gate=only_alternate_has_data, where no groundable Spec for the elected shape exists; alternate_match carries the substitute the engine found instead. Distinct from nearest_real, up to two constraint-RELAXED specs that DO have data nearby. flagged_match is the elected variable itself, unavailable as the request asked for it.

alternate_match.description: optional; a categorically different, data-bearing variable the request did not elect, present exactly when gate == 'only_alternate_has_data'. elected_count still counts the variable the request actually asked for; alternate_match is the one substitute the engine found nearby with observations of its own. Distinct from flagged_match (the elected variable itself, present on the other two gates) and from nearest_real (up to two constraint-relaxed variants of the SAME variable). alternate_match always names a different variable.

elected_count.description: optional; how many StatVars the request actually elected. Present whenever the elected shape's variable identity was graph-confirmed, whatever no_data reason or gate the outcome ultimately carries. None when the outcome stops short of a graph-confirmed identity altogether (variable_not_resolved, role_not_resolved, role_signature_incompatible, and binding_mismatch all resolve no StatVar to count). Counts the SAME variable as flagged_match whenever flagged_match is present. On gate=only_alternate_has_data, where flagged_match is absent, elected_count still counts the variable the request elected, distinct from alternate_match's different variable.
elected_count.title: Elected Count

entity_terms.description: the query entity text responsible for an entity-resolution outcome, in query order: every entity the engine could not resolve for entity_not_resolved, every ambiguous wording for entity_ambiguous, or every resolved-but-unadmitted entity for entity_role_not_admitted. Empty for every other no_data reason. This structured list is the client-facing source of those terms; rendered_sentence may quote the same wording for people, but clients must not parse it.
entity_terms.title: Entity Terms

ambiguous_entities.description: every ambiguous wording responsible for an entity_ambiguous outcome, in query order, each paired with the graph candidates it could name. Empty for every other no_data reason. Invariant: every group's `text` equals some restatement.entities[i].text on the same part. Additive to entity_terms, which carries the same wordings as bare strings; rendered_sentence is unaffected by this field and quotes the same wordings and candidate names for people, but clients must not parse it.
ambiguous_entities.title: Ambiguous Entities

source_terms.description: the source wordings responsible for a source-resolution outcome, in query order: every included wording that matched no admitted source for source_not_resolved, every ambiguous wording for source_ambiguous, and the part's source_code for source_code_not_held, source_code_ambiguous and source_code_shares_variable. Empty for every other no_data reason. rendered_sentence may quote the same wording for people, but clients must not parse it.
source_terms.title: Source Terms

ambiguous_sources.description: every ambiguous source wording responsible for a source_ambiguous outcome, in query order, each paired with the admitted sources it could name, and for source_code_ambiguous the part's source_code paired with the provenances holding it. Empty for every other no_data reason. A client posts the chosen candidate's ref on that mention of data_query, or for a source code as a new mention in its sources, and posts the part back.
ambiguous_sources.title: Ambiguous Sources

unit_alternatives.description: the currencies a unit_not_resolved outcome offers, in the binder's order: the candidate ISO codes for an ambiguous currency name with no declared alias (XOF, XAF and CHF for 'francs'), or the role shapes for a role-relative currency phrase beside entities on two roles. Absent on every other outcome, and on a unit_not_resolved outcome the binder offers no candidates for
unit_alternatives.title: Unit Alternatives

unbound_qualifiers.description: the ResolvedQualifier entries responsible for a qualifier_not_bound outcome, in query order: every entry from flagged_match.resolved.trace.query_qualifiers whose disposition is not "bound" ("unbound": a named code row exists but no final binding covers it; "no_vocabulary": the text names no code at all), then, for a part naming or leaving out sources, each source it could not bind, an "unbound" entry under the source's label whose named holds the source's references. Empty for every other no_data reason. This structured list is the client-facing source of which terms went unrecognised, alongside each one's own disposition; rendered_sentence may quote the same wording for people, but clients must not parse it.
unbound_qualifiers.title: Unbound Qualifiers

denominator.description: the denominator the question named and the one the flagged match divides by, set on every denominator_not_available refusal the engine returns after electing a series; null for every other no_data reason. A client can offer the flagged match, or fetch its nearest_real level and the denominator asked and divide them

data_query.description: the parsed form of this part, one part long, set when reason is entity_ambiguous, source_ambiguous or source_code_ambiguous: its variable text, entities with role_text, time, unit, sources, and operations. On entity_ambiguous every entity that resolved to one graph node is pinned to its dcid and each ambiguous wording left unpinned. A named group stays unpinned too, so it resolves to the same members again. On source_ambiguous every source mention that resolved carries its ref and each ambiguous wording carries none. On source_code_ambiguous it carries the code and the part's mentions. A client pins the candidate the user picks from ambiguous_entities or ambiguous_sources and posts the part back, through the parsed door or as a dataset_resubmit parsed entry. It is set when the part has no restatement too: an entity whose direction the question leaves unnamed carries no role_text. Null for every other no_data reason, and when the part's inputs exceed the ParsedPart bounds

NoDataDenominator.description:
The denominators a denominator_not_available refusal compared: the one the question
named and the one its flagged match divides by -- NoData.denominator.

asked.description: the denominator the question named, as the search read it from the bases the candidate series divide by; null when the question named none, or named one that no candidate series divides by

NoDataPart.description: Nothing could be returned for this part.

variable_text.description: the variable text this part answers, in the order asked. This part's position in Resolution.parts equals the same variable_index every SSE event keyed by variable_index uses (ShapeEvent, StepEvent, SentenceEvent). Every dataset_resubmit entry kind (identity, candidates, placeholder, and parsed through its nested ParsedPart) requires its own posted variable_text, so this field is always the posted text echoed back onto the rebuilt part, never null. Null only when the whole posted query was empty or whitespace-only (raw_text door), which refuses variable_not_resolved before extraction runs and so has no text to name.
variable_text.title: Variable Text

separate.description: true when this part was asked beside the others to be compared with them. A client resubmitting an identity, candidate set, or placeholder posts this flag on that entry to preserve the comparison. False, the default, is omitted
separate.title: Separate

warnings.description: this part's own run-health signals. A part folded into an earlier part's spec (see DefinitePart.spec) carries binding_folded alone. The merged spec's own resolved warnings live only on the first part that carries it. An unfolded part carries the warnings raised while resolving this part, plus observations_omitted on a candidates part when response_options.include_observations was set.
warnings.title: Warnings

timing_ms.description: this part's own latency breakdown, where by_step names only the phases this part ran and total sums them, leaving out the shape_* stages nested inside shape. Excludes the shared, once-per-request steps (e.g. extract), which diagnostics.timing_ms.by_step carries once for the whole request; distinct too from diagnostics.timing_ms.total, the whole request's wall-clock elapsed time.

rendered_sentence.description: a human-readable string. For candidates, a header naming how many readings there are ('3 readings.'), then each shown candidate's heading and a byline led by the source and span that set it apart; for no_data, a heading in the same claim form naming the entity, measure, and counterpart that were checked. Either ends with the text of this part's departures, in order. For a definite part this stays null or omitted: the confirmation sentence (heading and byline) lives at spec.resolved.rendered_sentence, and its departures reach the envelope's composed sentence.
rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence

sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, present whenever it is. For a definite part this stays null or omitted. spec.resolved.sentence_plan carries the confirmation sentence's own plan instead.
sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan

restatement.description: the ParsedPart that reproduces this part's own resolution inputs -- the same entities, resolved time window, unit text, and source text the engine actually used to resolve this one leg -- so a client holding this part alone can copy it straight into a fresh ParsedInput.parts entry and re-resolve it faithfully, without flattening it into the whole query's variable_text the way variable_text alone would. Canonical, not verbatim: for a raw_text part, time_text is the equivalent phrase this door's own time grammar recognises (e.g. '2015 to 2020'), not the user's original words, since the engine's date extraction keeps only the structured window and discards the phrasing. Null whenever this part has no faithful echo to give. On a dataset_resubmit entry's identity/candidates/placeholder kinds, which post an identity or stub rather than a phrase and have no per-part resolution inputs to echo -- a dataset_resubmit parsed entry, genuinely re-resolved from its own posted ParsedPart, carries a real one like any parsed-door part. Also null when this leg's entity was bound to a directional role axis (origin/destination) and no door-supplied role named that axis, since an echo without the axis would resubmit the request with that entity reversed. Also null when one of this leg's own inputs does not fit ParsedPart's own field caps, since a truncated echo would misrepresent what was actually resolved.

operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none
operations.title: Operations

departures.description: every way this part's answer differs from what its request asked, ordered by how much each changes the number: closest_match, measure_not_applied, operation_not_applied, breakdown_not_applied, entity_unavailable, year_unavailable, modelled_values, group_read_as_members, direction_discarded, direction_inferred, scope_limited. [] when the answer is what was asked. A client that renders its own sentence reads them here; each one's text also closes the sentence that carries this part (see Departure.text). A warning on the same part reports run health and stays separate
departures.title: Departures

ObservationsOmission.description:
Why a SpecObservations payload carries no series, made unconditional:
every _fetch_observations call that reaches a "nothing to show" outcome
sets this field instead of leaving the whole payload absent, so a client
is never left guessing which of at least a dozen distinct causes
produced an empty preview.

reason is a warning code from search.engine.region.codes (see
ObservationsOmissionReason's own docstring for the closed vocabulary and
why it is duplicated here rather than imported) -- the SAME code the
accompanying Warning carries when one is also emitted, so a client reads
one vocabulary rather than two. Not every reason accompanies a Warning:
a genuinely uninteresting omission (nothing was ever there to probe)
carries no diagnostic Warning of its own, but always carries this field.

The converse also holds, and the pairing is not exhaustive: a reason
arriving as a bare Warning with `omitted` absent means partial coverage,
not absence -- a fetch that delivered some series would never set this
field, but can warn (`observations_probe_failed` on a partially hard-
failed fetch, and `observations_timed_out` on one some of whose pairs
crossed the deadline).

Whenever `omitted` is set, SpecObservations.series is `[]`, total_obs is
`0`, and truncated is `false`, so a client reading `series ?? []` and
ignoring `omitted` sees an ordinary empty result, with no schema_version
bump needed to stay compatible.

pairs/cap: populated only for reason=="observations_preview_too_large" --
the (stat_var, role_tuple) pair (or pair x elected-combination
dispatch-item, or distinct-stat_var) count that was compared against the
ceiling it crossed, and that ceiling itself. Lets a client render "this
selection has {pairs} series, above the {cap} the preview fetches"
without re-deriving either number.

dispatched: how many (stat_var, role_tuple) pairs this call actually
dispatched. Populated for reason=="observations_no_points",
"observations_probe_failed", "observations_no_matching_source", and
"observations_timed_out" -- every reason a dispatch actually happened
for; None for a reason reached before dispatch (e.g.
"observations_nothing_to_probe").

empty: dispatched pairs that carried no data on their own facet.
Populated only for reason=="observations_no_points".

hard_failed: dispatched pairs whose fetch itself failed. Populated for
reason=="observations_no_points" (always 0 there -- a nonzero count
means reason is "observations_probe_failed" instead) and for
"observations_probe_failed" itself (the nonzero count that produced
that reason); None elsewhere.

facet_rejected: dispatched pairs a bound facet_filter (or currency
conversion) rejected. Populated for reason=="observations_no_points"
(always 0 there -- a nonzero count means reason is
"observations_no_matching_source" instead) and for
"observations_no_matching_source" itself; None elsewhere.

Every field left None where the branch that produced this omission has
no meaningful count for it.

reason.description: machine-readable cause, equal to the accompanying Warning's code when one fires
reason.title: Reason

message.description: human-readable explanation, safe to render directly
message.title: Message

pairs.description: observations_preview_too_large only: the count that was too large
pairs.title: Pairs

cap.description: observations_preview_too_large only: the ceiling it exceeded
cap.title: Cap

empty.description: observations_no_points only: dispatched pairs that carried no data on their own facet
empty.title: Empty

hard_failed.description: observations_no_points (always 0) and observations_probe_failed: dispatched pairs whose fetch itself failed
hard_failed.title: Hard Failed

facet_rejected.description: observations_no_points (always 0) and observations_no_matching_source: dispatched pairs a bound facet_filter rejected
facet_rejected.title: Facet Rejected

ObservationsOmission.title: ObservationsOmission

OpenAxisValueCount.description:
One declared value on an open constraint axis and how many served members
declare it (see OpenConstraintAxisFact.values).

count.description: how many distinct served members declare this value
count.title: Count

OpenAxisValueCount.title: OpenAxisValueCount

OpenConstraintAxisFact.description:
One constraint axis the query left open, and what this Spec's own
served StatVar members exhibit on it (see ResolvedSpec.open_axis_facts):
whether they agree on a single declared value or differ, what that
agreed value is when one exists, how many distinct values the axis
actually served, and how many declare none at all.

property.description: the constraint property dcid this fact is about
property.title: Property

varies.description: False when every served member that declares a value for this axis declares the same one (including when none of them declare one at all, since declaring nothing is itself an agreeing value here, the same rule resolved.alternative_measures' own observed-partition read applies); True when they differ
varies.title: Varies

value.description: the single value every served member that declares one for this axis agrees on; present only when varies is False and at least one member declares a value, absent when varies is True or every member declares nothing

distinct_count.description: how many distinct declared values the served members actually exhibit for this axis, not counting a member that declares nothing. 0 when every member declares nothing, 1 when varies is False and value is set. Counted over the served members' own declarations, independent of this response's observation window: a query's applied when-slot narrows which observation points are returned, not which constraint values a member declares, so this count is never scoped to that window the way an observation-count field on this contract is
distinct_count.title: Distinct Count

undeclared_count.description: how many served members declare no value at all for this axis. A member whose arc names the axis but never resolved to a dcid counts here too, the same as a member that never asserted the axis at all
undeclared_count.title: Undeclared Count

values.description: every declared value with the number of served members declaring it, highest count first, then by dcid. Each served StatVar counts once, also after a merge of answers that serve it more than once, so the counts plus undeclared_count sum to the distinct served members. Labels as for value
values.title: Values

Operation.description:
One computation the question asks for over a part's data, which search
does not perform: the part answers with the data the operation needs, and
the operation rides on the part for a client to perform or hand on.

verb.description: what the question asks to compute: rank, aggregate, growth, share_of, explain, forecast, or report
verb.title: Verb

phrase.description: the query wording that asks for the operation, e.g. 'top 5 donors'; one line with no control characters or line separators, and not blank
phrase.title: Phrase

over.description: the axis the operation runs across (place, origin, destination, category, or year); null when the verb names none, as explain does. The part leaves this axis open, so its data covers every value the operation needs
over.title: Over

target_year.description: the year a forecast projects to, e.g. 2050 for 'forecast aid to Ethiopia to 2050'; set only on a forecast, a four-digit year up to 2200. The raw_text door sets it only to a year after the current one, and leaves it null when the question names none; a posted value is taken as given within the bound, whatever today's date. It is kept apart from the part's time_text, the years whose data the part fetches, and does not affect resolution
target_year.title: Target Year

ParsedEntity.description: One entity mentioned in a parsed part, with an optional caller-supplied role hint.

text.description: the entity's text as the caller identified it
text.title: Text

role_text.description: the caller's free-form role hint for this entity, when available; recognised words (case-insensitive) are 'from'/'to' and synonyms such as donor/provider/funder/source/creditor/lender/exporter for the 'from' side, recipient/beneficiary/debtor/borrower/importer for the 'to' side -- unrecognised text warns role_text_not_recognised and the entity is treated as undirected
role_text.title: Role Text

dcid.description: an optional caller-pinned dcid for this entity, naming exactly which graph node `text` refers to -- the door a client with a candidate's dcid in hand (e.g. from NoData.ambiguous_entities) posts through, instead of relying on name resolution to disambiguate `text` on its own. When present, this entity's name resolution is skipped: the pinned dcid seeds the entry's pre_resolved map directly, still confirmed against the graph. An unconfirmable dcid (absent from the graph, or present but type-less) refuses invalid_role_ref (422). `text` stays required and is not re-derived from the dcid; it is still what a rendered sentence and any further restatement echo back.
dcid.title: Dcid

members.description: true asks for the members of the set `text` names, each as its own series: the countries of a continent or UN subregion, or the members of a group. It has no effect on a single place. Text whose wording names members, such as 'EU member states', reads as true without the flag. With a pinned `dcid` it is honoured for a continent or subregion that the membership policy holds or omits, whatever the node's graph type, and refuses request_invalid for a group's own node, whose members a pin cannot supply. One part names a set once: the same `text` posted with both values refuses request_invalid
members.title: Members

ParsedInput.description:
Pre-parsed input: one or more variable parts supplied directly by the caller,
skipping natural-language extraction.

parts.description: one entry per variable ask; conjunctions pre-split by the caller. Parts that are byte-identical across every field collapse to one before resolution, so the response's own parts list can hold fewer entries than this list.
parts.title: Parts

raw_query.description: original query text, for echo only; does not affect resolution
raw_query.title: Raw Query

ParsedInput.title: ParsedInput

ParsedPart.description: One variable ask within a parsed request, with its own entities, time, unit, and source.

variable_text.description: the variable's text as the caller identified it
variable_text.title: Variable Text

entities.description: entities associated with this part's variable, when available; null, omitted, or an empty list all mean no entity was named for this part, resolving the variable globally/entity-less -- the same meaning a raw_text query with no extracted place carries
entities.title: Entities

time_text.description: this part's time expression, when available; recognised forms include a bare four-digit year, 'YYYY to YYYY' or 'YYYY-YYYY', 'from YYYY to YYYY', 'between YYYY and YYYY', a latest end as in 'between YYYY and the latest' or 'YYYY to latest', 'since YYYY', 'latest', 'latest year available', 'most recent', and 'last N years'. Anything else resolves dateless with a time_text_not_parsed warning, whose message lists every form
time_text.title: Time Text

unit_text.description: this part's requested unit or measurement basis, when available; recognised phrasing names a currency (ISO 4217 code or curated name/alias), a price basis (current or constant prices), and/or a base year (e.g. '2015 US dollars', 'constant prices, 2015 base year'). A phrase this text failed to parse cleanly resolves no_data with unit_not_resolved; a phrase the request grammar cannot express at all resolves unsupported with unit_request_unsupported. A phrase the grammar CAN express is checked against this deployment's own unit data: a currency/prices/base_year combination no unit this deployment carries expresses at all resolves unsupported with facet_binding_unsupported; one this deployment can express but that matches no candidate observation resolves no_data with facet_not_available; a match resolves definite, applying the completed request to the resolved spec's identity and carrying request_basis on resolved.facets.unit
unit_text.title: Unit Text

sources.description: the data sources this part names or excludes, in query order. Empty, the part answers from the sources the engine elects. A restatement echoes each mention with the reference it resolved to
sources.title: Sources

source_text.description: deprecated: post `sources` instead. Read as one included mention with this text, appended to `sources`
source_text.title: Source Text

provenance.description: deprecated: post `sources` instead. Read as one included mention with this ref, appended to `sources`. The served request schema lists the code index's declared datasets under this field, each with its label, description and opt-in flag
provenance.title: Provenance

source_code.description: a publisher's own series code for this part's variable, such as the World Bank's DT.TDS.DEGG.CD, when the user or a skill gives one. Compared upper-cased, it names the variables the publisher gives that code, and the part answers from them in place of matching variable_text; variable_text, entities and open_roles still choose among them. A code is never a constraint and narrows nothing else. A code whose variables cannot answer the part, because no source search serves holds it, the part's sources leave out every source holding it, or its variables cannot answer the part as asked, resolves no_data with source_code_not_held, its message naming the cause; a code two of the part's sources hold resolves no_data with source_code_ambiguous until `sources` names one; a code whose variable another code of its source also names resolves no_data with source_code_shares_variable, naming those codes
source_code.title: Source Code

operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none
operations.title: Operations

open_roles.description: the roles this part asks for member by member, at most one word per flow axis, e.g. ['creditor'] for 'debt service paid to each creditor'. Each is a role_text word: creditor, donor, recipient, debtor, origin, destination, or a synonym. Where the answer's family declares the role, the answer holds one series per member of it and its identity states the axis in open_roles; a role named in neither entities nor open_roles reads as the total over that role. An unrecognised word, or a role one of this part's entities binds through role_text, refuses request_invalid. An operation whose over is origin or destination opens that axis too
open_roles.title: Open Roles

separate.description: true when this part is asked beside the others to be compared with them, as in 'health ODA versus education ODA': it answers as its own part and never folds into another part of the same shape (binding_folded). False, the default, folds parts that share a shape into one set answer
separate.title: Separate
