Resolution.description:
A resolve response that resolved the question into data: one part per
variable asked, in query order, each a complete outcome carrying its own
status and payload.

A single-variable query is one part, so `status` reads that one part's
status directly. A query in which extraction found no variable is also
one part, whose `variable_text` is the whole query text.

`status` below is a computed field that rides in every serialised
response body without being a settable input, so this class stays a
plain `BaseModel`, which allows unknown fields. `StrictModel` forbids them,
which would make `Resolution.model_validate` reject its own `model_dump()`
output, breaking every round-trip a client or this codebase does on a
fetched response body. A posted `status` is ignored and recomputed.

Usage::

    resp = RESOLVE_RESPONSE_ADAPTER.validate_python(obj)
    if resp.kind == "resolution":
        resp.status          # "definite" | "candidates" | "no_data" | "unsupported" | "mixed"
        resp.parts[0].status  # this part's own status

schema_version.description: contract schema version; exactly 1 for v1. Required on every response.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

query_echo.description: what the response was understood to be answering

diagnostics.description: run health, warnings, timing, build stamp

kind.description: discriminator for a response that resolved the question into data
kind.title: Kind

parts.description: one entry per variable asked, in query order
parts.title: Parts

rendered_sentence.description: the envelope-level confirmation sentence describing the whole query, composed across every part's own sentence in query order. When every contributing part is definite, their headings join into one sentence. A qualifier axis (where, when, or source, each a wire value of axis, plus origin, identified by role=='origin' instead since SentenceAxis has no 'origin' member) whose bound value agrees across every contributing part is stated once after the joined phrases, a possessive lead every part shares opens the sentence once, and the byline follows once. A qualifier that differs stays inline in each part's own phrase. The response falls back to one sentence per part, each part's own text left exactly as that part rendered it, when a part is still resolving, when the parts' bylines differ, or when a differing qualifier's connective opens with a comma (a period range). A part still resolving contributes up to three tokens of its own: an optional prefix text token, its own variable_text as an editable slot, and a text token stating the outcome. A lone part that is not definite composes to exactly that part's own sentence. After the headings and bylines, each part's departures follow in part order as segment='departure' tokens carrying that part's part_index. This is the one sentence that writes out a definite part's departures.
rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence

sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, present under the same condition; null or omitted otherwise. Composed the same way rendered_sentence is, from every part's own sentence_plan -- see SentenceToken.part_index for how a client recovers which parts[i] each variable phrase and attached qualifier belongs to, and which tokens are shared skeleton (an inter-phrase connective, a hoisted shared qualifier, the terminal '.', or the shared ' ' the per-part fallback puts between two sentences) rather than any one part's own.
sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan

skills.description: every skill named by any Spec.resolved.skills across this response's parts, keyed by id -- each id any Spec carries is a key here, and each key's front matter is carried once regardless of how many Specs name it. Present under response_options.include_skills; null when the option is off, {} when it is on and no Spec matched anything.
skills.title: Skills

status.description: the parts' shared status when every part agrees, or 'mixed' when two or more parts differ; derived from parts, never independently settable
status.title: Status

Resolution.title: Resolution

ResolutionTrace.description: Consolidated record of how the query was understood.

slot_filters.description: each applied bind decision, slot by slot
slot_filters.title: Slot Filters

query_qualifiers.description: each narrowing term the request's text named, and what became of it (see ResolvedQualifier). Defaulted empty: a dataset_resubmit identity entry carries no query text to re-derive this from, and every hand-built fixture and same-shape merge that predates this field still validates.
query_qualifiers.title: Query Qualifiers

requested_window.description: the date window originally requested (query intent), independent of coverage narrowing; None when no date was requested. The literal "latest" means the query explicitly asked for the most-recent/current value -- distinct from None (no date signal at all), since a resubmit of a "latest" spec must re-resolve to whatever year is CURRENTLY latest, not pin to the year this response happened to resolve. spec_id is anchored on this value, not on the served window, so identity stays stable across a resubmit even when coverage narrows the dates. Preserve the returned Spec.definition.identity when resubmitting; if editing it, carry this value at ResubmitIdentityPayload.identity.requested_window to keep that stability.
requested_window.title: Requested Window

capability_version.description: the deployment capability version that produced this Spec, shared verbatim with GET /api/search/capabilities and every problem-details body's own capability_version. None only in hand-built fixtures that predate this field; every engine-produced Spec populates it.
capability_version.title: Capability Version

default_reading.description: what the default price-basis reading did before bind (see TraceDefaultReading); None when no bind ran for this Spec, as on a resubmit, or in hand-built fixtures that predate this field

stated_form.description: the normalised form the quantity read found in the question when no wording pattern named one ("debt to GDP" asks for a rate), and which the answer was then checked against; None when a wording pattern named the form, when the question asks for none, and when no bind ran for this Spec
stated_form.title: Stated Form

conversion.description: always absent: conversion is recorded per series in resolved.observations.series[].conversion (see TraceConversion)

ResolutionTrace.title: ResolutionTrace

ResolvedEntity.description:
One resolved entity on the wire, under `resolved.entities`: the flat
projection of the engine's own `Entity` -- `ref`/`entity_type` collapse from
a `GraphRef` to a bare dcid/label pair, and `role` collapses from the
engine's richer role model to the role-key string it already derives from
(the identity core's own vocabulary, so this never adds a second mapping).

ref.description: the resolved entity's dcid
ref.title: Ref

label.description: plain-language display name
label.title: Label

role.description: the role key this entity plays; observationAbout, origin, or destination
role.title: Role

confidence.description: the engine's confidence in this entity resolution; None when not assessed -- no entity-resolution confidence signal exists yet, so this ships None on every entity today
confidence.title: Confidence

ResolvedEntity.title: ResolvedEntity

ResolvedFacet.description:
One facet axis's resolved value on a Spec (see ResolvedSpec.facets):
which value backed the answer's observations, and why.

basis is always present. ref/label are present when one distinct value
served every carried series; selection carries "per_series" in their
place when the carried series select different values on this axis --
never alongside ref/label. request_basis joins either shape, present
only on the unit axis, only when unit was bound through the request form
(currency/prices/base_year), one basis value per member the request
named.

Fields are flat and optional, validated by a model validator, rather
than a discriminated ref/selection union. basis and request_basis are
shared by both the single-ref and per-series shapes, so a union would
duplicate them across arms for a mechanical gain (moving the
ref/selection XOR to the type level) without expressing the
request_basis-only-on-unit constraint, since that constraint is about
which AXIS a ResolvedFacet lives under (see ResolvedSpec.facets), not
its ref/selection shape. This is also response-only data, never
deserialized from untrusted client bytes, so a runtime validator is
the right tool for catching an illegal engine-side construction.

basis.description: 'bound' when this axis was constrained by the request, 'declared_default' when an unbound axis was completed from a declared deployment policy, 'fallback' when neither applies and the deployment policy supplied the value: facets holding a point in the requested years first, then DFO's facets for a variable both DFO and base Data Commons hold, then the most places or role tuples covered there, then the most requested years the span covers, then most observations, then the latest observation, then a deterministic tie-break
basis.title: Basis

ref.description: the axis's resolved dcid, present when one distinct value served every carried series; absent when selection is 'per_series'
ref.title: Ref

label.description: best-effort display label for ref; present only alongside ref
label.title: Label

currency.description: unit axis only, alongside ref: the ISO 4217 code of the currency ref is denominated in, from the graph's currency units (CurrencyUSD, USDollar and the base Data Commons Currency members such as INR); absent when ref is no currency. The sentence reads it: US dollars go to the byline's unit token, any other currency stays in the heading
currency.title: Currency

source.description: provenance axis only, alongside ref: the organisation behind the provenance, from the origin catalogue

data_commons.description: provenance axis only, alongside ref: the Data Commons the provenance's data comes from

documentation.description: provenance axis only, alongside ref: the Graph API route of the provenance's document, GET /api/graph/documentation/{dcid}
documentation.title: Documentation

account.description: provenance axis only, alongside ref: whose account of a flow the provenance gives, when ref is a dataset the code index declares; 'provider' when it reports flows as their providers record them

selection.description: 'per_series' when the carried series select different values on this axis; present in place of ref/label, never alongside them
selection.title: Selection

request_basis.description: per-member basis (currency/prices/base_year) for a unit axis bound through the request form; present only on the unit axis, alongside either ref/label or selection
request_basis.title: Request Basis

ResolvedFacet.title: ResolvedFacet

ResolvedFilter.description: One applied bind decision, slot by slot.

refs.description: the bound graph objects (empty for unbound)
refs.title: Refs

provenance.description: whether the bind call's own election produced this value, a code row recognised in the query's own text forced it, or the measure-family election forced it on an axis the binder left open
provenance.title: Provenance

ResolvedFilter.title: ResolvedFilter

ResolvedQualifier.description:
One narrowing term the request's text named, and what became of it.

The term's text can come from the variable phrase, from the verbatim
`query_text`, or from an admitted qualifier tie (see
`_resolve_query_qualifiers`). `text` is the verbatim span of whichever
source named it. `named` is every code row -- any system -- that span
names in the packaged index;
empty when the text names no code at all (a `no_vocabulary` term). `slot`
is the constraint property dcid of the `slot_filters` entry whose
binding consumed the term, or, on an `"unbound"` value the answer's shape
has a slot for but leaves unmet, that slot's property; `None` otherwise.
`disposition` is
`"bound"` when some final binding on a named row's code system covers
it (that row or a descendant), `"unbound"` when a row was named but no
binding covers it, and `"no_vocabulary"` when the term names no code at
all -- an LLM-reported phrase (`bind`'s own `unplaced` output) that no
taxonomy in this deployment's index can express.

`start` and `end` locate the term in the part's variable phrase. `evidence` says what
read it, and `None` means a code's label or synonym matched the term as the query
spelled it, the reading every recognised span records:

- `"label"` and `"synonym"` name a match on a code's label or synonym; no record sets
  them, since a recognised span records `None`.
- `"model"` marks a phrase the bind model read through a code it chose from the
  phrase's candidate menu, a lexical hit of the menu or a descendant of one
  (`phase_rank_bind._model_records`); `named` holds the chosen codes.
- `"uncovered"` marks words no reader covers beside a recognised code
  (`phase_rank_bind._coverage_records`), recorded `"unbound"` with that code's rows as
  `named`.
- `"unavailable"` marks a code term the elected shape cannot apply: one naming only
  codes no shape can bind, or, on a part naming a dataset, one no row of that dataset
  holds (`phase_rank_bind._unavailable_qualifiers`), recorded `"unbound"`.
- `"unsupported"` marks an exclusion or comparison phrase no binding expresses
  (`phase_rank_bind._unsupported_records`), recorded `"no_vocabulary"`.

`operation` and `selected` describe how the term's codes combine with
another term's on one code system, and the codes it asked for before that
combination simplified.

text.description: verbatim span of the source text that named the term: variable_text, query_text, or a dropped qualifier phrase
text.title: Text

named.description: every code row the span names in the packaged index, any code system; empty when none did
named.title: Named

slot.description: property dcid of the slot_filters entry whose binding consumed this term, or, on an unbound value the answer's shape has a slot for but leaves unmet, that slot's property; None otherwise
slot.title: Slot

disposition.description: "bound" when a final binding covers a named row (or a descendant of one); "unbound" when a row was named but no binding covers it; "no_vocabulary" when the term names no code at all
disposition.title: Disposition

start.description: character offset where the term starts in the variable phrase
start.title: Start

end.description: character offset where the term ends in the variable phrase
end.title: End

evidence.description: what read the term: a code label or synonym, the bind model, "uncovered" for words no reader covers beside a recognised code, "unavailable" for a code no table holds, "unsupported" for a distinction no binding expresses
evidence.title: Evidence

operation.description: how the term's codes combine with another term's on one code system: a union of both, or a refinement to the narrower
operation.title: Operation

selected.description: the codes the term asked for before the combination simplified them
selected.title: Selected

ResolvedQualifier.title: ResolvedQualifier

ResolvedScope.description:
The full member set of an entity axis this Spec's request left unnamed
(see ResolvedSpec.scope).

``axis`` is observationAbout when place defaulting expanded a place-less
request, and origin or destination when directional-role defaulting
expanded a role-bearing request. ``members`` lists the entities on that axis
the answer's read plan serves, the ones a coverage breadth dimension for the
same axis counts. members is the single-element ["Earth"] list when the query
resolved as a worldwide total.
The response-level diagnostics may include place_scope_defaulted or
role_scope_defaulted for such resolution, but those warnings are not a
per-Spec one-to-one representation of this field. The scope lives outside
BaseIdentity, the spec hash, and resolved.entities: a resubmit of the
same definition rediscovers it from the live graph.

axis.description: the role-keyed axis the request left unnamed and the engine defaulted
axis.title: Axis

members.description: every entity on axis this Spec's read plan serves, sorted by ref; each carries role == axis and a best-effort label/entity_type from a batched graph read, None when the graph has neither
members.title: Members

ResolvedScope.title: ResolvedScope

ResolvedSpec.description:
What the graph held at resolution time: the engine's report of what it
did with the ask. Meant for display and diagnostics, never hashed;
`Spec.spec_id` depends only on `Spec.definition.identity`. Beside the
contract's own `resolved` member list (`stat_vars`, `inapplicable_slots`,
`unresolved_slots`, `entities`, `coverage`, `headline`, `facets`, `observations`,
`rendered_sentence`/`sentence_plan`, `slot_options`/`entity_options`,
`trace`, `confidence`), this also carries the engine's own supersets
(`shape`, `slots`, `available_at_place`) that slot_options/sentence_plan
join against and the eval harness scores.

slots.description: one entry per slot the shape defines, each in a binding state
slots.title: Slots

inapplicable_slots.description: the slots whose property none of the resolved StatVars declares, listed by property dcid; empty when every slot applies. Joins to resolved.slots[*].key.property.ref. Applicability is graph state, so it is reported here and the slot itself reads 'unbound' in the definition either way. It is never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.
inapplicable_slots.title: Inapplicable Slots

unresolved_slots.description: the slots whose property is present but unresolved on at least one resolved StatVar (the graph asserted a value for this axis but could not resolve it to a dcid), listed by property dcid; empty when no such slot exists. Joins to resolved.slots[*].key.property.ref, and is disjoint from inapplicable_slots: a property is either never asserted by any resolved StatVar (inapplicable_slots), present but unreadable on one (this field), or neither (a genuinely open axis). The slot itself reads 'unbound' in the definition in every one of these cases; it is never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.
unresolved_slots.title: Unresolved Slots

stat_vars.description: resolved StatVar(s) inside the region, and the scope they were drawn from

entities.description: resolved entities the data is about; may be empty if where is unbound
entities.title: Entities

entity_groups.description: the named group each role's entities stand for, keyed by the role key the entities above carry: each group whose members are exactly the entities definition.identity binds on that role. The heading names a role by its group and member count ('the 27 EU member states') in place of its members. None when no role was asked for as a group
entity_groups.title: Entity Groups

headline.description: exact latest-year summary for a role-bearing answer (see Headline); None for a non-role-bearing Spec, which coverage above already answers exactly or approximately enough that no separate latest-year summary is computed

download.description: the rows, series, years and licence of the file a mint of this Spec writes (see DownloadFacts). None when the Spec has no read plan: a no-data answer, or same-shape parts merged into one Spec

coverage_stamp.description: the coverage artifact's own data-version stamp this Spec's role-bearing population and headline were confirmed against (series_coverage.CoverageManifest.stamp); None for a non-role-bearing Spec, which never consults coverage. The graph-derived analogue of this stamp (graph_generation) is not itself a wire field; this is coverage's own, published because coverage is a second, independently-versioned data source an answer can be stale against
coverage_stamp.title: Coverage Stamp

scope.description: the full member set of an entity axis this Spec's resolution defaulted (see ResolvedScope): observationAbout for place defaulting, or origin/destination for directional-role defaulting. Response-level diagnostics may carry place_scope_defaulted or role_scope_defaulted, but warning presence is not an exact per-Spec equivalence; None when this Spec did not default an entity axis

facets.description: the facet axis values of the series this Spec's read plan serves, the series its observations carry (see ResolvedFacet); the same whether or not observations are included or deferred to a trailing SSE event. Sparse, meaning an axis no served series carries is omitted, never a null placeholder. {} when the Spec serves no series
facets.title: Facets

observations.description: the observation values behind coverage above; None when not resolved for this Spec (e.g. no entity to probe, or response_options.include_observations is false), when ResolveOptions.include_observations opts into deferred SSE delivery (populated instead via a trailing observations event, mirroring slot_options/entity_options' own coverage-probe transport split), or for a candidates-status entry, nearest_real, or flagged_match spec (this iteration only populates it on a primary definite answer).

slot_options.description: the candidate set each bound slot was chosen from, one entry per slot with a non-empty taxonomy; omits when/source and any slot with no observed or seeded values. spec_id does not depend on this field, so it never affects permalinks or dedup.
slot_options.title: Slot Options

entity_options.description: candidate sets for directional origin or destination axes. An entry whose entity_ref is omitted describes an axis the role-bearing query left open; its role selects the identity.entities key for a resubmit, and the matching role_axis_facts entry reports that axis's member count. An entry with an entity_ref describes alternatives to a bound axis. Empty when the family has no directional entity-option concept. spec_id does not depend on this field.
entity_options.title: Entity Options

facet_options.description: the candidate set each facet axis (provenance/measurementMethod/unit) was chosen from, one entry per axis with at least one value observed on the resolved candidates' unfiltered facets; an axis with no observed value is omitted, never an empty entry. Computed for every definite Spec and every candidate. Over SSE with response_options.include_option_coverage set, the entries arrive as trailing facet_options events and this list stays empty. Unlike slot_options, this has no bind-time baseline to fall back to. spec_id does not depend on this field.
facet_options.title: Facet Options

rendered_sentence.description: the editable confirmation sentence for this spec, present on every Spec a part shows; None on an equivalent_readings entry. It holds the heading and the byline only (see SentenceToken.segment): 'Germany's gross ODA disbursements to Kenya, 1973 to 2024. Current US dollars · OECD Creditor Reporting System (CRS).' It states what this Spec is and nothing about the request that produced it, so it reads the same after a dataset_resubmit and serves as the Spec's label. The part that carries this Spec states how it departs from the request (_PartBase.departures)
rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence

sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, tying its tokens to definition parts; present under the same condition, None otherwise. Every token's segment is 'heading' or 'byline'
sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan

trace.description: consolidated record of how the query was understood

confidence.description: qualitative, relative retrieval confidence for this interpretation; None when not assessed. Bands are heuristic and may be retuned without a schema-version bump.
confidence.title: Confidence

basis.description: why the part offers this Spec as one of its candidates: 'structural', a reading that differs from the elected one only on a stat type, price basis or denominator the request leaves open; 'nominated', a reading the model named as a genuine reading of the request's phrase; 'twin', an equivalent reading of the elected one, offered where the elected one holds no data; 'direction', the same reading with the other direction for a place the request names without one, which a client shows as a direction prompt. The elected reading, listed first, carries none. None on a definite answer and on every Spec outside CandidateSet.specs.
basis.title: Basis

available_at_place.description: whether this spec has lifetime availability at the resolved place, independent of the coverage window. True = confirmed at place; False = the variable matched but has no observation here (the flagged_match case); None = not assessed (no place entity, or a named family such as dev-finance). CoverageExact.has_data may be False for a requested window even when this field is True.
available_at_place.title: Available At Place

equivalent_readings.description: other StatVar(s) confirmed to encode the same real-world indicator as this Spec. Each entry is a full Spec carrying identity and the material needed to re-resolve onto it: its definition.identity, spec_id, and resolved StatVar dcids provide everything ResubmitIdentityPayload requires. Its rendered_sentence, sentence_plan, facet_options, and observations come from re-resolving onto it on a dataset_resubmit identity entry, not from this response. This Spec's own answer stands on its own regardless. Switching to a named entry is optional, offered for its source vocabulary's own coverage. None when no such encoding is known. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed, and never populated on its own entries in turn. An entry's own equivalent_readings is always empty.
equivalent_readings.title: Equivalent Readings

skills.description: ids of the skills this Spec's bound graph nodes and selected provenance call for, matched against the shared skills index, most specific first: skills matched through a graph node by hop, then breadth, and skills matched only through the provenance last; present under the include_skills option. None = the request did not ask; [] = it asked and nothing matched.
skills.title: Skills

alternative_measures.description: every other measure this Spec could equally answer with -- either another populated partition from the same family as the one this Spec's own served rows exhibit (retrieval.bound_values.observed_measure_family), or a genuinely distinct also_plausible candidate whose only difference from this Spec is measured_property (measurement_denominator held equal), folded in here instead of left as a second candidates entry -- each with its own identity, a disambiguating label, and the axis of the sentence token whose menu offers it: 'what' entries are the measure switch beside measure_label below, 'unit' entries the price-basis options of the byline's unit token (binding_ref 'unit:'). A partition or folded candidate with no authored label is left out. None when this Spec's shape carries no measure family at all and no measure-sibling candidate was folded in, or its served rows span more than one partition; a served partition with every sibling unlabelled, or with none, still publishes []. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.
alternative_measures.title: Alternative Measures

measure_label.description: the readable label for the measure partition this Spec's own served rows exhibit, composed the same way as each 'what' alternative_measures entry's label: what a switch built from those entries would show as currently selected. It names no price basis ('gross disbursements', not 'gross disbursements (nominal)'). Current or constant prices belong to the unit, which the byline's unit token states. None under the same condition alternative_measures is None
measure_label.title: Measure Label

measure_label_axes.description: the declared measure-axis identifiers (code_index.types.MeasureAxis.axis, e.g. 'measuredProperty', 'measurementQualifier', or a constraint-property dcid such as a financial-flow-type or netting-basis axis) that measure_label was composed from. Every axis the served partition carries a value on is included here, whether or not its value appears in measure_label's own text. A renderer uses this to keep a bound how-slot sharing one of these property dcids from repeating what measure_label already said. Always [] when measure_label is None.
measure_label_axes.title: Measure Label Axes

measure_axis_values.description: each axis in measure_label_axes with the value the served partition holds on it, in the same order, including values the query never named (a declared default such as Gross or Nominal). Labels come from the measure index. Always [] when measure_label is None. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.
measure_axis_values.title: Measure Axis Values

related_group.description: the StatVarGroup related_measures come from: the smallest group this Spec's one StatVar belongs to that holds 2 to 40 members, ties broken by group dcid. None when related_measures is None or []

related_measures.description: up to 5 other members of related_group with data at every place this Spec names (and in its requested years when it names a range), ordered by the years they share with this Spec's StatVar there, then by dcid. Only a definite Spec that serves exactly one StatVar, has no measure family (measure_label is None) and names places with no roles carries a list; [] when no group qualifies or no other member has data there. None for any other Spec, and when the graph reads failed or ran past their deadline. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.
related_measures.title: Related Measures

open_axis_facts.description: one entry per constraint axis this Spec's own served StatVar members declare (an arc naming the property, resolved or not) that the query left unbound, each naming the axis's property and what those members exhibit on it: whether they agree on a value (varies=False) or differ (varies=True), and undeclared_count for how many declare none at all. None when this Spec's served members declare no constraint property the query left open at all. This is distinct from an open axis every member declares nothing for, which still publishes its own entry (varies=False, undeclared_count equal to the served member count). Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.
open_axis_facts.title: Open Axis Facts

role_axis_facts.description: one entry per directional role axis (origin/destination) this role-bearing Spec's query left open, naming the axis and the member population its own confirmation already resolved (see RoleAxisFact). None when this Spec is not role-bearing, or is role-bearing but every role axis its shape declares carries a bound entity. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.
role_axis_facts.title: Role Axis Facts

unit_conversion.description: the currencies and price bases a unit request can convert this answer to. Null when the served members' unit is no currency, no conversion recipe converts them (a stock, a series not in nominal prices, or a provenance that declares no recipe), the recipe's tables lack the native currency's rate in a served year, so nothing converts, or no conversion catalogue is loaded, which the part's unit_conversion_unavailable warning states. Never a member of BaseIdentity, never hashed.

ResolvedSpec.title: ResolvedSpec

ResolvedStatVars.description:
`resolved.stat_vars` on the wire: how many StatVars the answer holds, how many a
Datasets mint of the Spec's definition serves, and the dates the answer serves over
them. The members themselves stay off the wire; `POST /api/datasets/{id}/members`
lists the ones a mint serves.

member_count is the population confirmed to carry observations at this
resolve's own probe entities, not resolved.shape.member_count's
bindings-admitted population. The two differ for two reasons. A member the
shape's bindings admit can carry no observation at the resolved place. And on
a role-bearing shape the answer reads one role class of the admitted members:
where a total stands for its breakdowns the breakdowns are folded into it, so a
donor-only answer can state 255 admitted members beside 1 confirmed while every
one of the 255 holds data. On a standard (non-role-bearing) shape this population can itself
be a floor: the packaged code index does not source members for every
shape family, so a shape outside it falls back to its recall sample, the
members recall found, and member_count cannot exceed what that sample
admitted. An answer naming one member of a family too large for one read stops
reading once that member is confirmed, so member_count counts the members read: "latest
life expectancy data" reads the family's total and not its other 350 members. A
where-axis merge (same_shape.py, "population
of Kenya and Uganda") publishes max() of its members' own member_count
rather than the sum, since the same StatVar is typically confirmed at
every member's own place and summing would double-count the
intersection -- max() is a true lower bound of the union. member_count_exact
records which of these applies.

served_count is the mint's own count, a function of the definition alone: the
StatVars a Datasets mint of `definition` serves, the length of its
`trace.resolved_stat_vars`. It is stated whenever Search settled the membership the
mint resolves: a family the code index decides, or a family the mint's member walk
settled for this definition. Null when Search answers from members it could not
settle, which the part flags with a `membership_unverified` warning.

member_count.description: how many members are confirmed to carry observations at this resolve's own probe entities; see this model's own docstring for how this differs from resolved.shape.member_count
member_count.title: Member Count

member_count_exact.description: True when member_count is a true total; False when it is a floor -- the population being at least member_count large, not exactly member_count -- because it was measured over a capped recall sample, because the probe stopped once the answer's member was confirmed, or because it is a where-axis merge's max() of its members' own counts rather than a computed union. Defaults to True, correct for a caller that has not measured otherwise
member_count_exact.title: Member Count Exact

served_count.description: how many StatVars a Datasets mint of this Spec's definition serves, the length of its trace.resolved_stat_vars; 1 for a single series. Null when the membership is unsettled: Search answered from members the mint may not serve, and the part carries membership_unverified
served_count.title: Served Count

data_date_range.description: the earliest first date and latest last date of the points the answer's read plan serves over its StatVars; null when it serves none

source_codes.description: the publisher series codes of the StatVars the answer serves, sorted by provenance then code and without repeats; left out when no served StatVar has a code. They identify the series a publisher files these StatVars under, and the answer is the same with or without them. A code names the whole answer only where its entry is exact
source_codes.title: Source Codes

ResolvedStatVars.title: ResolvedStatVars

RoleAxisFact.description:
One directional role axis (origin or destination) a role-bearing
Spec's query left open, and what this Spec's own confirmation already
knows about its member scope (see ResolvedSpec.role_axis_facts).

Unlike OpenConstraintAxisFact, a role axis has no declared value of its
own that could vary across served members -- the axis is a place a flow
entity binds, not a constraint members assert -- so this carries no
varies/undeclared_count of its own; it carries only what a role axis
genuinely has: a population size and whether that population is known.

SentenceToken.description:
One token in the ordered sentence plan: a "text" token (invariant
wording such as a connective, a bare separator, the terminal period, or a
departure sentence) or a "slot" token (a slot- or entity-bound phrase, or
the wording of an ambiguous entity).

``rendered_sentence`` (the flat string) is the plain concatenation of every
token's ``text``, in order. The two are computed together and cannot drift.
A "slot" token with nothing bound appears too, with ``text=""``: the same
token structure serves a loading skeleton (before binding is known) and the
final sentence (after it is). The first non-empty token's text is
capitalised.

Every token belongs to one ``segment``. The heading states what the answer
is: actor, measure noun, counterpart, and period, in possessive order, one
slot token per axis ("Germany's gross ODA disbursements to Kenya, 1973 to
2024"). A unit that changes the magnitude (per capita, percent of GDP, PPP
international dollars) stays in the heading. The byline follows it: the
latest-year label when one applies, the plain unit with its price basis
("current US dollars", "constant 2022 US dollars") as a slot token with
axis "unit", the source, and, when the identity binds measurementMethod, the
method as a slot token with axis "method". Departures come last and sit only on a part's or
the envelope's sentence, so ``spec.resolved.sentence_plan`` carries none.

kind.description: 'text' is invariant wording: a connective carrying its own surrounding whitespace (' for ', ' to '), a possessive suffix ("'s"), a bare ' '/', ' separator, the terminal '.', or a departure sentence; 'slot' is a slot- or entity-bound phrase, or on an entity_ambiguous no_data plan the ambiguous wording itself, which a client hangs the candidate menu on. A client that does not recognise a kind should render its text as plain text regardless.
kind.title: Kind

text.description: the rendered text for this token; empty string for a slot with nothing bound
text.title: Text

axis.description: the grammatical axis this token fills, when kind=='slot': one of the request-slot axes, 'unit' for the byline's unit of measure, or 'method' for the byline's measurement method, which no request slot carries. The unit token's binding_ref is 'unit:', and its options are the Spec's resolved.alternative_measures entries with axis 'unit': the price-basis siblings (current and constant prices) where the graph holds both. The method token appears only when the identity binds measurementMethod (a ref, a null ref, or a set), after the source token; its binding_ref is 'method:', its text the bound method's label without a trailing full stop or 'No stated method' for a null ref, and its options the Spec's facet_options entry with axis 'measurementMethod'
axis.title: Axis

segment.description: the part of the sentence this token belongs to: 'heading' (what the answer is), 'byline' (latest-year label, unit, source, and a bound method), or 'departure' (the text of one Departure on the same part, never on a Spec's own plan). A client styles each segment as a block; the plain join of every token's text still equals rendered_sentence
segment.title: Segment

property_dcid.description: the constraint property dcid this token renders, when one exists; null or omitted for property-less axes (when/source), for a shape-label fallback phrase with no backing slot, and for entity-role tokens with no backing where slot. Set on a 'destination' entity-role token when the shape declares a where slot backing that axis (e.g. dev-finance).
property_dcid.title: Property Dcid

role.description: origin/destination when this token renders a directional entity role (the flow's two endpoints read back), or the directional scope an unbound where slot resolved to. entity_refs is the discriminator: non-empty on the entity read-back, empty on the unbound-where-slot fallback. binding_ref is not: an entity read-back carries binding_ref too whenever the shape declares a where slot backing the 'destination' axis (e.g. dev-finance), the same condition under which the unbound-where-slot fallback always carries it, so a present binding_ref value never separates the two. Both kinds join to the Spec.resolved.entity_options entry on the same role. A third token sits on an entity_ambiguous no_data plan, which has no Spec: the ambiguous wording, with the role the request gave it (null when it gave none), no entity_refs and no binding_ref, and text equal to one NoData.ambiguous_entities[i].text on the same part. The client titles that wording's candidate menu by this role and pins the pick into NoData.data_query.

binding_ref.description: join key correlating this token to its Spec.resolved.slots / SlotOptions entry: 'axis:property_dcid', i.e. SlotKey.as_ref() (matching Slot.key and SlotOptions.key). Set for a slot-backed token, and also for a 'destination' entity-role token when the shape declares a where slot backing that axis (e.g. dev-finance) -- see entity_refs for the entity side of that token. The byline's unit token carries 'unit:', which no slot backs; its options are the resolved.alternative_measures entries with axis 'unit'. The byline's method token carries 'method:', which no slot backs either. Null or omitted for plain connective text, a shape-label fallback phrase with no backing slot, and 'origin'/unbacked-'destination' entity-role tokens.
binding_ref.title: Binding Ref

entity_refs.description: entity dcids this token renders, set on the entity read-back, one of the two token kinds role marks (see role's own docstring for the other, the unbound-where-slot fallback, which leaves entity_refs empty even though it too carries role) -- a directional entity read-back has no Spec.resolved.slots entry of its own, though a 'destination' token may additionally carry binding_ref when a backing where slot exists (e.g. dev-finance); one dcid per entity in the token's group, in the same order as the entities joined into this token's text -- e.g. a 'destination' token reading 'Ethiopia, Kenya, and Uganda' carries all three dcids, so a client can tell a 3-entity answer from a 1-entity one without parsing rendered text. Empty when role is unset, and this emptiness, not binding_ref, is the join rule that separates the two role-bearing kinds.
entity_refs.title: Entity Refs

states.description: the refs a heading or byline slot token states, so a client edits each from this token: its own binding_ref, then each binding the renderer left silent because this token's text already says it. Refs read as binding_ref does ('how:crsTypeOfFlow', 'where:', 'origin:', 'unit:'), plus 'axis:<property dcid>' for a measure axis no slot carries ('axis:nettingBasis'). The measure noun states the measure axes its label or authored noun carries, the how values it names, and the agreed open axes beside it; a StatVar name or graph name states the how values it folds. The byline's unit token states 'unit:' and, when it names a price basis, the measurementQualifier axis. The byline's source token states 'source:', which is also its binding_ref where the answer binds a source slot. The byline's method token states 'method:', its binding_ref, and while the identity binds no method no token states 'method:'. Empty on a token with empty text, on text tokens, and outside heading and byline slot tokens. Within one part, no ref appears on two tokens with text. A bound slot, an unbound slot with options, or a role that no token states is stated nowhere in the sentence (a boolean member, an adjectival fold dropped whole, an open role with no count), and a client offers it apart from the sentence with its current value. On the envelope plan a token with no part_index states its refs for every part it stands for
states.title: States

distinguishes.description: true when this token's text differs from the same-bucket text on another candidate in the same CandidateSet; null or omitted on every other token, including every token on a Spec rendered outside a candidate set
distinguishes.title: Distinguishes

part_index.description: this token's position in Resolution.parts, when this plan is the envelope-level composed sentence (Resolution.sentence_plan) and this token belongs to exactly one part's own contribution -- a variable phrase token, or a qualifier attached to it because it did not agree across every part, or a token of a part composed as its own sentence. Null carries three distinct readings a client must not conflate: on a part's own plan (DefinitePart.spec.resolved.sentence_plan, or the candidates/no_data/unsupported sentence_plan on _PartBase) the field has no meaning at all and is never set; on a composer-minted connective, it means the token belongs to the sentence as a whole rather than to any one part (the Oxford-joined ' and '/', ', the plan's own terminal '.', and the shared ' ' the per-part fallback puts between two sentences are all such tokens); and on a token every contributing part states alike and the join states once (a hoisted qualifier on the where, when, or source axis, each a wire value of axis, or the origin role, identified by role=='origin' instead since SentenceAxis has no 'origin' member; a shared possessive lead; the shared byline; or a heading or byline token of a part a later part folded into, binding_folded, which both parts state) it means the token no longer describes a single variable.
part_index.title: Part Index

SpecAlternativeMeasure.description:
One other measure this Spec could equally answer with (see
ResolvedSpec.alternative_measures): either another populated partition
from the same family as the one this Spec's own served rows exhibit, or
a genuinely distinct also_plausible candidate whose only difference from
this Spec is measured_property (measurement_denominator held equal),
folded in here instead of left as a second candidates entry. Carries its
own identity and a label that disambiguates it.

`definition` is minted by editing this Spec's own already-minted
identity onto this partition's measure axes (retrieval.bound_values.
mint_sibling_identity), an index-scan projection, not a resolution.
Carries identity and a label only: no stat_vars, no coverage, no trace.
ResolvedSpec's own required fields have no defaults, so producing one as
a Spec would mean fabricating a resolution that never ran.

switch onto this measure: the identity's own what/how slots (this
partition's per-partition-declared axes included, e.g. CRS cooperation
modality) name the family the packaged code index's own election
recovers members from, the same recovery a resubmit of this Spec's own
identity uses.

that differs from this Spec's only in price basis (`measurementQualifier`

byline's unit token (binding_ref "unit:"). Every other entry is a measure
option, axis "what". The measure menu holds one entry per measure
whatever its price basis, so no two "what" entries differ only in price
basis.

SpecObservations.description:
The observation values behind a Spec's coverage.

An opt-in bounded preview, or the full series when the resolved answer is
small enough to ship in full -- see truncated. Describes the SAME (stat_var,
entity) selection Spec.resolved.coverage already reports, so the numbers here never
describe a different variable than what coverage summarises.

Each series carries one lead observation facet's points, never a union
across facets: a StatVar/entity pair can have several reporting facets
(e.g. commitments vs disbursements, current vs constant prices), and
merging their points chronologically would interleave same-dated points
from incompatible series into one meaningless line. The one exception is
the same source's estimates continuing the lead past its last period: the
series carries their points after the lead's, `facet` names the lead, and
the `modelled_values` departure marks the estimates. One facet group is
selected per StatVar instead, across every place and role tuple the answer
names: among facets holding a point in the requested years (all facets when
none does), DFO's facets first for a variable both DFO and base Data
Commons hold, then the one covering the most places or role tuples there,
then the most requested years, then the most observations, then the latest
observation, then a deterministic tie-break.

series.description: one entry per (stat_var, role tuple) pair with observations
series.title: Series

total_obs.description: total observation count across every series' SELECTED facet, window-filtered to the spec's requested window when one exists -- known even when truncated is true and points are truncated. For a windowed per-pair answer, this is the chosen facet's in-window point count, NOT a raw facet obs_count sum and NOT a union across every facet of the pair -- see ObservationSeries. For a scope-defaulted bulk latest-only answer (no requested window), this sums the coverage probe's all-time obs_count per delivered entity instead: with no window to narrow it, that raw obs_count IS the in-window count
total_obs.title: Total Obs

truncated.description: false when every series above carries its FULL point set (the whole answer's point count was within the server's inline threshold and each series within its row limit); true when a series was truncated to its latest points only, its total_obs still counting every point
truncated.title: Truncated

omitted.description: why this payload carries no series, when it doesn't; absent when series is genuinely populated. See ObservationsOmission's own docstring

order.description: how a role-bearing bulk preview chose the series it shows when it shows fewer than the answer holds: 'ranked' when it read every series and shows the most recent and largest (latest year, then latest value, then identity), 'fixed' when it shows a selection made before any value was read, StatVars newest year first and taken round-robin; absent when every series is shown or the preview is not a role-bearing bulk one
order.title: Order

SpecObservations.title: SpecObservations

TimeWindow.description: A date window. Absence of a bound means open-ended in that direction.
TimeWindow.title: TimeWindow

Timing.description:
Latency breakdown, reused at two scopes: the envelope's own
diagnostics.timing_ms, where total is the whole request's wall-clock
elapsed time and by_step names the steps that run once per request,
shared across every part (e.g. extract), and a part's own timing_ms,
where total sums that part's own by_step values and by_step names only
the phases that part ran, excluding the shared steps already reported
on the envelope. A part's shape_arcs, shape_probe, shape_probe_coverage,
shape_labels, shape_groups and shape_admission steps are nested inside
its shape step, so its total leaves them out.

total.description: total latency in milliseconds, at whichever scope this sits
total.title: Total

Timing.title: Timing

TraceConversion.description:
A Spec-level record of a unit-conversion recipe. The engine converts
per series and records each converted series' recipe and tables in
ObservationSeries.conversion, since one Spec's series can convert under
different recipes. ResolutionTrace.conversion is modelled here but always
absent. Capabilities.recipe_classes lists the recipe members this
deployment applies.

recipe.description: the conversion recipe class that ran
recipe.title: Recipe

input_tables.description: the input series/table dcids the recipe combined, keyed by role
input_tables.title: Input Tables

TraceConversion.title: TraceConversion

TraceDefaultReading.description:
The default price-basis reading applied before bind. Price bases rank Nominal,
RealValue, InflationAdjusted, then PurchasingPowerParity, with any basis the query names
moved first. A StatVar leaves the menu when a StatVar of a better-ranked basis with the
same constraints holds data wherever it does over the requested years. The trace records
whether the step ran and the StatVars it removed.

applied.description: false when a phrase the request dropped uses a price-basis word no qualifier match read, so every price basis stayed on the menu and the alternate guard applied no default reading
applied.title: Applied

removed_stat_vars.description: the StatVar dcids the default reading removed; empty when it removed none
removed_stat_vars.title: Removed Stat Vars

TraceDefaultReading.title: TraceDefaultReading

UnitAlternative.description:
One currency a unit_not_resolved refusal offers in place of the unit
phrase it could not resolve -- one entry of NoData.unit_alternatives.

currency.description: the value a caller resubmits as facets.unit.request.currency, as written: an ISO 4217 code for an ambiguous currency name, or a role shape for a role-relative currency phrase beside entities on two roles
currency.title: Currency

label.description: the currency's display name, or the role's reader-facing noun
label.title: Label

UnitAlternative.title: UnitAlternative

UnitConversion.description:
The conversions a unit request can ask of this answer: the currencies, years and base
years the conversion recipe of its served members converts. A request posts one as the
identity's `facets.unit` (`IdentityFacetValueRequest`).

currencies.description: each currency a unit request accepts that converts at least one served year at current prices, at a constant-price base year, or both, sorted by code
currencies.title: Currencies

default_base_year.description: the base year a constant-price request that names none completes to: the deflatorBaseYear every conversion table declares
default_base_year.title: Default Base Year

role_currencies.description: the ISO 4217 code of the national currency (the graph's nationalCurrencyOf arc) of the one entity bound on each role, among `currencies`. A role bound to several entities, or to one no single currency names, is absent. A request may name the role ({'role': 'origin'}) or the code
role_currencies.title: Role Currencies

UnitConversion.title: UnitConversion

Unsupported.description:
The request was valid and fully understood, but not supported.

Fires for a text-door condition the request grammar or this deployment
cannot honour: the unit binder recognises but cannot represent a unit
phrase at all -- PPP terms, per-capita, a percent/share unit, or a scale
word (million/billion/thousand) -- code unit_request_unsupported, or a
recognised facet axis this deployment cannot bind (code
facet_binding_unsupported). A unit phrase the request form COULD
represent, but that this text failed to parse cleanly (two conflicting
currencies, price bases, or base years in one ask; an incomplete "base
year" cue with no year value), is a different outcome entirely: it lands
no_data with reason unit_not_resolved, never here. Distinct from every
refusal: the request was never malformed or unresolvable, so this is a
200, not a problem-details body.

code.description: the reason, a code from the platform registry
code.title: Code

pointer.description: a JSON Pointer into `definition` (not the request body) naming the binding at fault -- a text-door request has no structured body to point into
pointer.title: Pointer

cause.description: why this refusal fired, present only for code=recipe_not_declared (the structured door's same-named ProblemDetails extension); omitted on every other code

definition.description: the canonical definition as interpreted -- {schema_version, identity: {identity_version, shape, slots, entities, facets, requested_window}} -- without spec_id, since this was never a resolvable construction
definition.title: Definition

Unsupported.title: Unsupported

UnsupportedPart.description: This part's variable was valid and understood, but not supported.

variable_text.description: the variable text this part answers, in the order asked. This part's position in Resolution.parts equals the same variable_index every SSE event keyed by variable_index uses (ShapeEvent, StepEvent, SentenceEvent). Every dataset_resubmit entry kind (identity, candidates, placeholder, and parsed through its nested ParsedPart) requires its own posted variable_text, so this field is always the posted text echoed back onto the rebuilt part, never null. Null only when the whole posted query was empty or whitespace-only (raw_text door), which refuses variable_not_resolved before extraction runs and so has no text to name.
variable_text.title: Variable Text

separate.description: true when this part was asked beside the others to be compared with them. A client resubmitting an identity, candidate set, or placeholder posts this flag on that entry to preserve the comparison. False, the default, is omitted
separate.title: Separate

warnings.description: this part's own run-health signals. A part folded into an earlier part's spec (see DefinitePart.spec) carries binding_folded alone. The merged spec's own resolved warnings live only on the first part that carries it. An unfolded part carries the warnings raised while resolving this part, plus observations_omitted on a candidates part when response_options.include_observations was set.
warnings.title: Warnings

timing_ms.description: this part's own latency breakdown, where by_step names only the phases this part ran and total sums them, leaving out the shape_* stages nested inside shape. Excludes the shared, once-per-request steps (e.g. extract), which diagnostics.timing_ms.by_step carries once for the whole request; distinct too from diagnostics.timing_ms.total, the whole request's wall-clock elapsed time.

rendered_sentence.description: a human-readable string. For candidates, a header naming how many readings there are ('3 readings.'), then each shown candidate's heading and a byline led by the source and span that set it apart; for no_data, a heading in the same claim form naming the entity, measure, and counterpart that were checked. Either ends with the text of this part's departures, in order. For a definite part this stays null or omitted: the confirmation sentence (heading and byline) lives at spec.resolved.rendered_sentence, and its departures reach the envelope's composed sentence.
rendered_sentence.title: Rendered Sentence

sentence_plan.description: the ordered token form of rendered_sentence, present whenever it is. For a definite part this stays null or omitted. spec.resolved.sentence_plan carries the confirmation sentence's own plan instead.
sentence_plan.title: Sentence Plan

restatement.description: the ParsedPart that reproduces this part's own resolution inputs -- the same entities, resolved time window, unit text, and source text the engine actually used to resolve this one leg -- so a client holding this part alone can copy it straight into a fresh ParsedInput.parts entry and re-resolve it faithfully, without flattening it into the whole query's variable_text the way variable_text alone would. Canonical, not verbatim: for a raw_text part, time_text is the equivalent phrase this door's own time grammar recognises (e.g. '2015 to 2020'), not the user's original words, since the engine's date extraction keeps only the structured window and discards the phrasing. Null whenever this part has no faithful echo to give. On a dataset_resubmit entry's identity/candidates/placeholder kinds, which post an identity or stub rather than a phrase and have no per-part resolution inputs to echo -- a dataset_resubmit parsed entry, genuinely re-resolved from its own posted ParsedPart, carries a real one like any parsed-door part. Also null when this leg's entity was bound to a directional role axis (origin/destination) and no door-supplied role named that axis, since an echo without the axis would resubmit the request with that entity reversed. Also null when one of this leg's own inputs does not fit ParsedPart's own field caps, since a truncated echo would misrepresent what was actually resolved.

operations.description: the operations the question asks for over this part's data, in query order; the engine echoes them onto the part it resolves. Empty when the question asks for none
operations.title: Operations

departures.description: every way this part's answer differs from what its request asked, ordered by how much each changes the number: closest_match, measure_not_applied, operation_not_applied, breakdown_not_applied, entity_unavailable, year_unavailable, modelled_values, group_read_as_members, direction_discarded, direction_inferred, scope_limited. [] when the answer is what was asked. A client that renders its own sentence reads them here; each one's text also closes the sentence that carries this part (see Departure.text). A warning on the same part reports run health and stays separate
departures.title: Departures

UnsupportedPart.title: UnsupportedPart

Warning.description:
A run-health signal. Note: this name shadows the Python builtin Warning.

Only `observations_series_truncated`, `elected_shape_no_data` and `un_system_unavailable`
set `params`. A `None` `params` is left out of every dump, so other codes' warnings stay
exactly `{code, severity, message}` plus `spec_id` where one applies.

code.description: stable machine code from the platform registry, lower snake_case, e.g. date_coverage_partial, binding_folded
code.title: Code

spec_id.description: the spec_id this warning attaches to, when it concerns one returned spec specifically; omitted otherwise
spec_id.title: Spec Id

params.description: the counts and labels the message states, for a client to compose its own text. observations_series_truncated: {shown, total, order}, the series shown, the confirmed series behind them, and how the shown series were chosen: 'ranked' (the most recent and largest) or 'fixed' (a selection made before values were read, not ranked by value). elected_shape_no_data: {no_data, elected}, the labels of the readings with no data and of the readings answered instead. un_system_unavailable: {places, variables, variable_labels}, the place dcids the UN front door refused, the variables of the UN reads that failed, each empty when none, and each variable's graph name, in variables order, '' where the graph holds none; a warning without params says the UN search itself was unavailable. Omitted for every other code
params.title: Params

Warning.title: Warning
